newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Novartis unit plans new products.
newsitem.headline: German Novartis unit plans new products.

text.p: Novartis Deutschland GmbH, the German unit of Swiss drugs giant Novartis AG, said on Tuesday it plans to secure its leading position in the German market with new products and possible acquisitions.

"Novartis Deutschland is the number one life sciences group in Germany and we plan to strengthen our position further by focusing on innovative technologies and products," Dieter Wissler, president of Novartis Deutschland, told reporters.
Silvio Gabriel, the group's head of pharmaceuticals, said Novartis' ongoing strong drugs research should allow the group to launch two to three new products annually.
"Our pipeline stands up favourably in comparison to others and we expect to make two to three new launches per year."
Gabriel declined to say how these new products would impact either Novartis AG or Novartis Deutschland GmbH's results, saying only that the group "plans to grow faster than the market average."

Sales and profit forecasts would be extremely difficult to make, Gabriel said, adding these often depended on the kind of drug that was launched. "Heart/circulatory drugs are sure to post higher sales than cancer medicines," Gabriel said.
At the same time Novartis Deutschland, fresh from acquiring generic drug group Azupharm from Gehe AG last year, may consider rounding out its product offerings with acquisitions.
"Right now we see that our product palette is fairly well covered with Azupharm but we could consider rounding out the product palette with another acquisition," Gabriel said.
Currently generic products, the cheaper versions of products whose patent protection has expired, make up 11 percent of Novartis Deutschland's total turnover.
Novartis last year posted sales of 2.8 billion marks ($1.69 billion) with the health sector making up the lion's share of 70 percent, Wissler said.
The group posts 64 percent of its sales in pharmaceuticals, 13 percent in consumer health, and 12 percent with Ciba Vision.

Novartis Deutschland last year edged past Hoechst Marion Roussel to become Germany's leading life sciences group (pharmaceuticals, generics, consumer health) capturing a 5.8 percent market share after Ciba-Geigy AG and Sandoz AG merged.

Hoechst Marion Roussel, the drugs unit of German chemicals giant Hoechst AG, posted 5.5 percent market share, topping Bayer AG's 3.8 percent and privately-held Boehringer Ingelheim's 3.4 percent market shares in 1996.
Earlier today, Novartis AG posted 1996 sales of 36.2 billion Swiss francs.
